limits: No experiments or measured results; all numbers are illustrative or guideline values.
Display equations (loss, basic GNN update, mean/symmetric normalisation, GAT attention weights) are not in the text layer.
Listings 11.2-11.7 are sketches (e.g. MultiHeadGraphAttention sets head_dim=input_dim while chunking features) and are not run.
The GraphSAGE section says attention is integrated in aggregation, which does not match GraphSAGE's aggregators.
Karate club result is qualitative only.
practices: Consider non-Euclidean (hyperbolic) embeddings only with strong evidence of hierarchical structure (11.1.1).
Use inductive methods when new nodes are expected; transductive for static graphs (11.1.1).
Use negative sampling with cross-entropy, 5-10 negatives per true triple, gamma > 1 (11.4.1).
Filter accidental true edges from random negatives; prefer type-constrained or adversarial sampling; corrupt head, tail or both (11.4.1).
Pick the KG decoder by relation patterns: TransE for composition, ComplEx for asymmetry (11.4.2).
Use normalisation when features matter more than structure or degrees vary widely; it is lossy (11.6.1).
Use skip connections, gated updates or jumping knowledge to avoid over-smoothing and feature loss (11.6.4).
